recheck.evidence_quote: Free plan: 1000 calls per workspace per month (Team: 100,000; Business/Enterprise: unlimited, subject to rate limits). — Airtable support, "Managing API call limits in Airtable"
recheck.notes: Verified on vendor pages: the dev docs intro describes a REST-style JSON API ("closely follows REST semantics"). Personal access tokens are created self-serve at airtable.com/create/tokens (pick scopes and bases, token shown once, sent as Authorization: Bearer). The PAT page doesn't state plan requirements. Free-plan access comes from the support article https://support.airtable.com/docs/managing-api-call-limits-in-airtable, via a search summary. I did not fetch that article directly, so re-check the exact wording. The summary says the free plan gets 1,000 API calls per workspace per month, with a one-time 30-day grace period. Team gets 100,000. Business and Enterprise are unlimited, subject to rate limits. Integration traffic counts against the same quota. Rate limits (5 req/s per base, 50 req/s per token/user) are from the earlier record and the search summary, and Airtable says they may change. A newer vendor page, https://airtable.com/developers/web/api/billing-plans, and a rule effective Aug 10, 2026 (Viewer (Restricted) users can't write via the API, including with PATs) were seen only in search results, not read. The old record's "free-plan access inferred" caveat can be replaced with the 1,000-call monthly cap, which is the practical limit for free users. Not checked: GraphQL, webhooks, and the full endpoint list. Webhooks are likely but unverified.
